task.title: Relics: share relics through origin
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

This story shares relics through `origin` the way tasks are shared. After it, a relic created in one clone is readable in another, including a brand new one.

## What this delivers

- Relic refs are fetched and pushed in the same step as task refs, by every command that syncs today: the automatic sync on each mutation, `fetch`, `push`, `sync`, the sync watcher, and `setup` on a fresh clone.
- Every relic mutation publishes itself, as task mutations do, and honors `--no-sync` and the `auto-sync` setting.
- A sync checks only the relics that changed since the last one. An unchanged relic costs one line in the list of refs that `origin` sends.
- Syncing reads `state.json`, `links.json` and the sizes of the part objects. It does not read body text.
- A folder that holds only Workbook data and no code holds relics too. Tests cover that setup.

## When two edits meet

A push that is refused because someone else got there first replays the pusher's unpublished changes on top of what it fetched, then pushes again, as for tasks.

| What both sides changed | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Different parts, different fields, or different properties | Both apply. Nothing is reported. |
| The same field or property, to different values | The later sync wins, as for a task's fields today. Both edits stay in history. |
| The title, or the position of the same part | The later sync wins. |
| The same body | A conflict. The command stops and returns the starting version, the local version and the other version. Automatic merging is a later story. |
| One side removed a part and the other edited it | Both apply. The part stays removed and keeps the edit. The sync warns that an edit landed on a removed part. |
| One side deleted the relic and the other edited it | A conflict, as for a deleted task today. |

- Workbook never stores conflict markers or a half-merged value.
- A conflict uses the existing conflict exit code and report shape, extended to name the part.
- The agent resolves a conflict by reading the current version and saving again from it.

## Teammates on an older Workbook

- An older version only asks `origin` for task, settings and project refs. It never fetches relics, so it neither shows them nor breaks on them.
- Tasks do not change format, so an older version keeps full use of tasks.
- Tests prove both, using the previous release's fetch behavior against a remote that holds relics.

## Done when

- Two clones and a bare remote pass every row of the table above in integration tests.
- A fresh clone and a tasks-only folder both receive every relic from `setup`.
- Retried and duplicated deliveries leave the same state.
- Task sync timings are unchanged when no relic changed.
- The architecture document describes relic refs, the fetch and push rules, and the mixed-version behavior.

## Not in this story

Automatic merging of body text, links, schemas and the index.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
